'''Andrei Andreevich Bolibrukh''' ({{langx|ru|Андрей Андреевич Болибрух}}) (30 January 1950 – 11 November 2003) was a [[USSR|Soviet]] and [[Russia]]n [[mathematician]]. He was known for his work on [[ordinary differential equation]]s especially [[Hilbert's twenty-first problem]] ([[Riemann–Hilbert problem]]).<ref name="Kang">{{cite journal|doi=10.1070/RM2004v059n06ABEH000792|last=Anosov|first=D. V.|author2=V. P. Leksin|year=2004|title=Andrei Andreevich Bolibrukh in life and science |journal=Russ. Math. Surv.|volume=59|issue=6|pages=1009–1028|bibcode=2004RuMaS..59.1009A}}<!--|accessdate=2009-08-01--></ref> Bolibrukh was the author of about a hundred research articles on theory of [[ordinary differential equations]] including [[Riemann–Hilbert problem]] and [[Isomonodromic deformation#Fuchsian systems and Schlesinger's equations|Fuchsian system]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ems-ph.org/books/050/preface_9783037190203.pdf |title=IRMA Lectures dedicated to the memory of Andrei Bolibrukh |access-date=2018-03-17 |archive-date=2016-08-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160807042456/http://www.ems-ph.org/books/050/preface_9783037190203.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Work==
Bolibrukh was born on 30 January 1950 in [[Moscow]] and studied at the [[45th Physics-Mathematics School]] in [[Saint Petersburg]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Выдающиеся выпускники |url=http://agym.spbu.ru/gimnaziya/vydayushchiesya-vypuskniki.html |website=Notable Alumni of the Academic Gymnasium}}</ref> After receiving his mathematical education at the [[Lomonosov Moscow State University]], with [[Mikhail Postnikov|Mikhail Mikhailovich Postnikov]] and Alexey Chernavskii as thesis advisers, he started working on the proof of the existence of linear differential equations having a prescribed [[Monodromy|monodromic group]]. He applied modern methods of [[complex analytic geometry]] to classical problems about [[ordinary differential equation]]s and was an expert on [[Hilbert's twenty-first problem]]. In 1989, Bolibrukh produced his famous counterexamples which invalidated the [[Josip Plemelj]]'s 1908 solution of Hilbert's twenty-first problem.<ref>{{cite book
|author=Bolibrukh, A. A.
|title=21st Hilbert Problem for Linear Fuchsian Systems
|publisher=Amer Mathematical Society
|year=1995
|isbn=978-0-8218-0466-7}}</ref> Bolibrukh dedicated much of his efforts to the Riemann-Hilbert problem in order to find full necessary and sufficient conditions for given [[Isomonodromic deformation#Monodromy data|monodromy data]] to be those of a Fuchsian system.

During his short career he served as Deputy Director of the [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]] and professor at the [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]].<ref>[http://math.fizteh.ru/kafedra/staff.esp Chair of Mathematics, MIPT] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090728004040/http://math.fizteh.ru/kafedra/staff.esp |date=July 28, 2009 }}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
In 1994 Bolibrukh was elected to the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]]. He was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in Zürich in 1994.<ref>{{cite book|author=Bolibruch, A. A.|chapter=The Riemann-Hilbert problem and Fuchsian differential equations on the Riemann sphere|title=''In:'' Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians|pages=1159–1168|publisher=Birkhäuser Basel|year=1995|doi=10.1007/978-3-0348-9078-6_45|isbn=978-3-0348-9897-3|citeseerx=10.1.1.462.4938}}</ref> He was awarded the Lyapunov Prize from the Academy of Sciences, Russia in 1995. In 2001 Bolibrukh received the [[State Prize of the Russian Federation]].
